audits.title: P3 A closed loop audit on pre-operative anaemia in major elective orthopaedic surgery
audits.standard: International consensus statement on perioperative anaemia: treat Hb <130 before elective surgery

cycle1.result: 38% underwent arthroplasty with Hb <130; 14% with Hb <120; 11% of anaemias appropriately investigated; 7% had attempted treatment.

audits.intervention: Results presented at clinical governance meeting; departmental action plans for early identification and treatment of anaemia to Hb 130, delaying operations where necessary.

cycle2.result: 21% operated with Hb <130 (p = 0.036); 0% with Hb <120; 80% of anaemias appropriately investigated (p < 0.001); attempted treatment 20% (p = 0.279).

audits.other_findings: Increase in attempted anaemia treatment before surgery was not significant.
audits.citation: Koh C, Gruner-Hegge N, Ignatov D, Shakir A. P3 A closed loop audit on pre-operative anaemia in major elective orthopaedic surgery. BJS Open. 2021;5(Suppl 1).

audits.title: Effect of a patient blood management programme on preoperative anaemia, transfusion rate, and outcome after primary hip or knee arthroplasty: a quality improvement cycle.
audits.standard: National agency instruction to implement blood conservation measures including preoperative anaemia management
audits.setting: Airedale NHS Foundation Trust (UK general hospital); primary hip or knee arthroplasty

cycle1.result: Preoperative Hb predicted allogeneic blood transfusion (odds ratio 0.25 per 1 g/dl)

audits.intervention: Patient blood management algorithm adapted for UK practice to optimise Hb before arthroplasty and limit perioperative Hb loss

cycle2.result: Associated with improved outcome up to 90 days after discharge; figures not given in the supplied text

audits.other_findings: Retrospective audit group served as control for the prospective audit.
audits.citation: Kotzé A, Carter LA, Scally AJ. Effect of a patient blood management programme on preoperative anaemia, transfusion rate, and outcome after primary hip or knee arthroplasty: a quality improvement cycle. Br J Anaesth. 2012;108(6):943-952. doi:10.1093/bja/aes135. PMID: 22593128.

audits.title: Preoperative Anemia Screening and Treatment Practices in Patients Having Total Joint Replacement Surgery: A Retrospective, Observational Audit.
audits.standard: National Blood Authority Patient Blood Management guidelines: FBC, iron studies, CRP and renal function at least 6 weeks before surgery, with treatment of anaemia
audits.setting: Four campuses (three private, one public) of a tertiary metropolitan healthcare facility, South East Queensland; primary total hip and knee replacement

cycle1.result: FBC 96% (583), renal 94.7% (575/607), iron studies 8% (49/607), CRP 2.4% (15); all recommended tests 2.4% (15). Screening 6 weeks or more before surgery 3.95% (24/607). 85 (14.6%) anaemic; 10/85 had some preoperative treatment and 1.2% (n = 1) received guideline-concordant treatment.

audits.other_findings: Anaemic patients were more likely to be transfused (OR 8.65) and stayed one day longer; 21/40 (52.5%) transfusion episodes did not follow PBM guidance. A standardised anaemia pathway was being developed.
audits.citation: Delaforce A, Galeel L, Poon E, Hurst C, Duff J, Munday J, et al.. Preoperative Anemia Screening and Treatment Practices in Patients Having Total Joint Replacement Surgery: A Retrospective, Observational Audit. J Blood Med. 2020;11:259-265. doi:10.2147/jbm.s254116. PMID: 32821186.

audits.title: 73 An Audit Evaluating the Management of Pre-Operative Anaemia in Elective Bowel Resections at Frimley Park Hospital
audits.standard: National and local guidelines recommending treatment of preoperative anaemia
audits.setting: Frimley Park Hospital, elective bowel resection

cycle1.result: 29 anaemic; 16 (55%) received iron, all intravenous and none mildly anaemic; median Hb rise 14 g/L.

audits.other_findings: Median stay 6 days with normal Hb vs 8 days with anaemia; only one patient normalised Hb.
audits.citation: Coyle M, Rangarajan K, Celera S, Dowson H, Nizar A. 73 An Audit Evaluating the Management of Pre-Operative Anaemia in Elective Bowel Resections at Frimley Park Hospital. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_2). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab134.360.

audits.title: 521 Optimising Anaemic Patients for Colorectal Cancer Surgery: Implementation of Day-Case Iron Infusion Pathway and Closed Loop Audit of Anaemia Management in Colorectal Cancer Patients
audits.standard: NICE recommendation to screen for and treat anaemia; local guideline advocating pre-operative IV iron via day-case unit
audits.setting: Elective colorectal cancer surgery, Royal Derby Hospital

cycle1.result: 27.5% (11/40) anaemic; 18% (2/11) received pre-operative iron infusion; 45% (5/11) of anaemic patients had post-operative transfusion.

audits.intervention: Departmental education on anaemia management and further publicity of the day-case iron infusion pathway.

cycle2.result: 45.4% (20/44) anaemic; 60% (12/20) received iron infusion; 20% (4/20) of anaemic patients required post-operative transfusion.

audits.other_findings: None of the cycle 1 transfused patients had pre-operative IV iron, and 3 of 4 transfused in cycle 2 had not received it.
audits.citation: Malcolm F, Kaji F, Shelswell L, Plummer B, Speake W, Liptrot S, et al.. 521 Optimising Anaemic Patients for Colorectal Cancer Surgery: Implementation of Day-Case Iron Infusion Pathway and Closed Loop Audit of Anaemia Management in Colorectal Cancer Patients. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab259.061.

audits.title: EP.WE.385A retrospective audit reviewing current practice on managing the incidence of anaemia and iron deficiency in pre-operative oesophagogastric resection patients
audits.standard: NICE: patients with anaemia should be offered iron therapy before and after surgery
audits.setting: Tertiary care centre, Norfolk and Norwich University Hospital, oesophagogastric resection

cycle1.result: Preliminary: 71% had haemoglobin <130 g/l (men) or <120 g/l (women), but only 6.7% received any preoperative iron therapy.

audits.intervention: Planned intervention to raise pre-operative haemoglobin, followed by repeat audit (not yet done).
audits.other_findings: 42.8% of patients had a post-operative complication.
audits.citation: Bhatti S, Evans L. EP.WE.385A retrospective audit reviewing current practice on managing the incidence of anaemia and iron deficiency in pre-operative oesophagogastric resection patients. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_7). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab308.046.
